Tables 6–7 verify all 48 copied comparison numbers, including the literal, inconsistent Translation V2T median rank of 56.1. The later CVPR version updates the How2Sign baselines and does not match the values copied into CiCo.

status.numerical_agreement_basis: All 24 in-scope released-checkpoint evaluation targets produced comparable values. At the prospectively declared one-decimal precision, all eight PHOENIX values match; two How2Sign recalls differ by +0.1 percentage point, and six CSL-Daily recalls differ by -0.6 to +0.1 points. All median ranks match. This evaluates released checkpoints, not training reproducibility.

observations: Tables 1–3 were visually verified on PDF page 7. Table 2's copied Translation V2T median rank of 56.1 is preserved literally despite being inconsistent with an ordinary median of integer ranks. CSL discrepancy investigation: the source and data content are unchanged from the original 0322431 release; later CiCo changes concern file modes and the README. The fixed released checkpoint, both exact feature sets, all 1,176 labels, official alpha 0.8, default batch size 256, seed 42 and metric implementation were used. No material protocol mismatch was found. Environment drift or differences between the released checkpoint and the one behind the published table remain possible but unproven.

How2Sign discrepancy check retained the official released checkpoint, 2,348 paired features, 1,969 query groups, alpha 0.8, seed 42, batch 256 and unmodified metrics. Only T2V R@1/R@5 differ by +0.1 percentage point. No demonstrated protocol defect or score-driven change was made.

claims.claim: CiCo substantially outperforms the reported SPOT-ALIGN retrieval baselines on How2Sign and PHOENIX.
claims.paper_evidence: Section 4.2, Tables 1–2 (PDF page 7), and Section 5 (PDF page 8).
claims.basis: Against the published SA-COMB rows, evaluated How2Sign T2V/V2T R@1 gains are +22.5/+28.0 percentage points; PHOENIX gains are +13.7/+17.1. Recall@5/10 ordering is also preserved. PHOENIX median ranks tie the SA-COMB baseline. The baseline systems were not rerun.

claims.claim: The released method provides a retrieval baseline on CSL-Daily.
claims.basis: Evaluated T2V/V2T R@1 are 75.1/74.8 and both median ranks are 1. Table 3 supplies no competing system, so this does not establish superiority on CSL-Daily.

claims.claim: The training procedure and proposed components cause the reported gains.
claims.paper_evidence: Section 4.3, Tables 4–9, and the training claim in Section 4.2.
claims.basis: This attempt evaluates released checkpoints and features. It does not repeat training, component ablations, baseline training/evaluation, or multiple training seeds.

conclusion_assessment.limits: No new numerical tolerance or statistical significance criterion is introduced. Evaluation of one released checkpoint per dataset cannot estimate training-seed variability or establish end-to-end training reproducibility.
